rules: RANK or ZSCORE of a single fundamental leaf (e.g. RANK($roa)) is too shallow to ever pass crossover_not_a_fusion as a whole-tree parent, since the entire donor is just that one small fragment. Caused 5 of this round's rejections, all pairing RANK($roa) with a second subtree. Embed such leaves in a larger expression before using them as a crossover parent.

The high-low range normalized by $open or $dollar_volume motif is over-mined: three crosses/window-variants of this same pair were all rejected this round for overlapping an existing archive member. Rest this family for a few rounds.

Cosmetic re-wraps of archived winners (adding CS_DEMEAN, nudging a window slightly, or swapping CS_RANK for CS_ZSCORE) keep failing for overlapping the parent too closely, three times this round, including two variants of the best-performing overnight-gap factor. Extend winners with new fields or real sub-expressions, not outer wrapper changes.

Same-field price momentum (return-sum differences, price-to-own-MA ratios, new-high counts) failed the cheap screen standalone across every window tried this round, 5 to 120 days. The same return-sum idea passed once fused from the start with a zscored fundamental (asset_turnover). Pair weak momentum candidates with a fundamental at proposal time rather than screening them standalone.

This round's best factor is a cross-field ratio of open to prior close, not a same-field trailing-return construct. Favor overnight or cross-field price relationships over same-asset momentum ratios and sums.

A bare rank of a single fundamental's raw multi-month delta, with no price or volume interaction, also failed the cheap screen this round. Fundamentals need a richer transform or an interaction partner, not just rank-of-delta.

Reordering RANK and TS_MEAN around $dollar_volume, rank then smooth vs. smooth then rank, produced a near-duplicate of the plain smoothed version already known. Not a source of novelty for slow-moving, cross-sectionally stable fields.

In the close-position-in-range family, the denominator's ceiling term must stay $high, not $close; swapping it in this round destroyed most of the parent's IC. Preserve the $high and $low pairing when varying or simplifying this family.
